results.location: 2. Materials and methods — animals and experimental design
results.content: 6. A total of sixty rats were allocated into five groups, with each group consisting of twelve rats, using a random assignment method. Group 1 (sham) comprised of rats that received a sham operation. Group 2 (BDL) comprised of rats that underwent BDL. Group 3 (BDL/quinacrine 5) consisted of rats that underwent BDL followed by intraperitoneal (i.p.) administration of quinacrine (5 mg/kg/day) for 28 days. Group 4 (BDL/quinacrine 10) consisted of rats that received BDL, thereafter quinacrine was injected i.p. (10 mg/kg/day) for 28 days. Group 5 (quinacrine 10/sham) consisted of rats that received a sham operation, thereafter quinacrine was injected i.p. (10 mg/kg/day) for 28 days. Quinacrine was dissolved in distilled water (freshly prepared) and injections began on the same day as the surgery. A priori power analysis was performed utilizing G*Power (version 3.1.9.7, Heinrich-Heine University, Germany) to determine the requisite total sample size for the proposed experimental model. The analysis was conducted with an alpha error of 0.05, a power level of 0.85, and an effect size of 0.5. A total sample size of 60 animals (12 each group) was established based on these criteria. The experimental design is illustrated in (Fig. 1).
results.route_rationale: An a priori power calculation for a one-way ANOVA. The verdict needs the noncentral F distribution, which is out of practical reach in Lean/Mathlib; checked numerically instead.

fallback_result.reasoning: Two checkable claims. (a) Allocation arithmetic: $5 \times 12 = 60$, so "sixty rats ... five groups ... twelve rats" is internally consistent. (b) The a priori power analysis: for a one-way ANOVA with $k = 5$ groups, $\alpha = 0.05$ and Cohen's $f = 0.5$, the noncentrality parameter is $\lambda = f^2 N = 0.25N$ with $\mathrm{df}_1 = 4$, $\mathrm{df}_2 = N - 5$. Evaluating $1 - F_{\mathrm{nc}}(F_{0.95,4,N-5}; 4, N-5, 0.25N)$ gives power $0.8526$ at $N = 59$ and $0.8598$ at $N = 60$, so the smallest admissible $N$ is $59$ and the smallest multiple of $5$ (equal group sizes) is $60$. The reported total of $60$ animals, $12$ per group, is exactly what G*Power returns for these inputs. No error.

results.content: apart and each rat was then placed in the box and allowed to explore for a duration of 5 min. On the 29th day (test day), the animals were reintroduced inside the test box, to which a new object was added in place of one of the objects that they had previously been familiar with. Rats were allotted for a duration of 3 min to investigate the objects, and the duration of exploration for each object was documented using the overhead camera. The cumulative duration of investigating both the known and unfamiliar objects was computed. In addition, the discriminating index was computed as the difference in the amount of time consumed examining familiar and novel things, divided by the overall exploration time of both objects [26].
results.route_rationale: A definition whose sign convention can be checked against the direction of the reported results; no formal content for Lean beyond a sign.

fallback_result.reasoning: As literally worded the index is $\mathrm{DI} = (T_{\text{familiar}} - T_{\text{novel}}) / (T_{\text{familiar}} + T_{\text{novel}})$ — "the difference in the amount of time consumed examining familiar and novel things, divided by the overall exploration time of both objects". With that order of subtraction the BDL group, whose novel-object time is 26.4% *below* its familiar-object time, would have a **positive** index, and the quinacrine groups (novel above familiar, 1.23- and 1.49-fold) would have **negative** ones. That is the opposite of what Section 3.3 reports ("BDL rats showed a notable decrease in the discriminating index ... (BDL + quinacrine 5) group demonstrated a notable improvement"). The standard NOR convention, and the one evidently used in the figures, is $(T_{\text{novel}} - T_{\text{familiar}})/(T_{\text{novel}} + T_{\text{familiar}})$. The quantity is well defined and bounded in $[-1, 1]$ either way, so the defect is a reversed order of subtraction in the prose rather than an invalid computation; it does not propagate into any reported number. Not flagged as a critical mathematical error.

results.content: Two measurements were taken: the escape latency during the 4-day training period (days from 25 to 28) and the duration of each rat’s presence in the targeted region during the 2-min probe experiment. Concerning the duration of escape latency, rats receiving BDL spent significantly more time 1.6- and 2-fold longer, respectively, on comparing to the sham group during the third and fourth days. In contrast, in (BDL + quinacrine 5) and (BDL + quinacrine 10) treated groups, quinacrine resulted in a considerable reduction of the escape latency by 23% and 45.7%, respectively, opposed to the BDL group. Co-administering quinacrine at dosage 10 mg/kg led to notable reduction in escape latency by 27.4% and 47%, respectively. There was no noticeable distinction observed in the escape latency between the two doses of quinacrine (Fig. 2D).
results.route_rationale: The second pair of percentages has no identifiable antecedent, so no faithful formal statement can be written; this needs a reader's judgement, not the kernel.

fallback_result.reasoning: The passage prints four percentages whose comparators cannot be pinned down. "[Q]uinacrine resulted in a considerable reduction of the escape latency by 23% and 45.7%, respectively, opposed to the BDL group" fixes $L_{Q5} = 0.77\,L_{BDL}$ and $L_{Q10} = 0.543\,L_{BDL}$ — pooled across days. The next sentence, "Co-administering quinacrine at dosage 10 mg/kg led to notable reduction in escape latency by 27.4% and 47%, respectively", gives a bare "respectively" with no antecedent pair. Two readings are possible and both are problematic. (i) If the two numbers are days 3 and 4 for 10 mg/kg vs BDL, they cannot be reconciled with the single 45.7% already given for that comparison. (ii) If they are 10 mg/kg vs 5 mg/kg, then the first two figures force a between-dose reduction of $1 - 0.543/0.77 \approx 29.5\%$ (29.88–30.89% once the rounding of 23% and 45.7% is allowed for), which excludes the printed 27.4%; and a "notable reduction" of 27.4–47% between doses sits badly with the closing sentence "There was no noticeable distinction observed in the escape latency between the two doses of quinacrine". Because the referents are genuinely undetermined I cannot convert either reading into a confident error claim, so this is recorded as unsettled rather than flagged.

results.content: During the probing trial, the BDL group spent 56.57% less time in the desired quadrant than the sham group. The target quadrant time was 1.46- and 1.86-fold longer in the (BDL + quinacrine 5) and (BDL + quinacrine 10) treated groups, respectively, compared to the BDL group. Furthermore, a significant difference existed between the two dosages; quinacrine (10 mg/kg) markedly extended the duration in the target quadrant by 1.27-fold compared to (BDL + quinacrine 5) (Fig. 2E).

Reported: `T_BDL = (1 - 0.5657) * T_sham`, `T_Q5 = 1.46 * T_BDL`,
`T_Q10 = 1.86 * T_BDL`, and `T_Q10 = 1.27 * T_Q5`.
The between-dose figure is determined by the other two.
-/

theorem mwm_probe_between_dose_consistent
    (Tsham TBDL TQ5 TQ10 : ℝ) (hsham : 0 < Tsham)
    (hBDL : TBDL = (1 - 5657/10000) * Tsham)
    (h5 : TQ5 = 146/100 * TBDL)
    (h10 : TQ10 = 186/100 * TBDL) :
    TQ10 / TQ5 = 93/73 ∧ |TQ10 / TQ5 - 127/100| < 5/1000 := by
  have hB : 0 < TBDL := by rw [hBDL]; nlinarith
  have hQ5 : 0 < TQ5 := by rw [h5]; positivity
  have hval : TQ10 / TQ5 = 93/73 := by
    rw [h10, h5]; field_simp; ring
  refine ⟨hval, ?_⟩
  rw [hval]
  rw [abs_lt]; norm_num

/-- Robust to the printed rounding: any `f5 ∈ [1.455,1.465]`, `f10 ∈ [1.855,1.865]`
still gives a between-dose ratio that rounds to the printed `1.27`. -/

    (f5 f10 : ℝ) (h5 : |f5 - 146/100| ≤ 5/1000) (h10 : |f10 - 186/100| ≤ 5/1000) :
    |f10 / f5 - 127/100| < 15/1000 := by
  rw [abs_le] at h5 h10
  have hpos : 0 < f5 := by linarith [h5.1]
  exact ratio_abs_lt hpos (by nlinarith [h10.1, h5.2]) (by nlinarith [h10.2, h5.1])

findings.exact_quote: In addition, the (BDL + quinacrine 10) treated group showed a considerable increase in the expression of WNT3A, β-catenin, and Lef1 (1.45-, 1.98-, and 1.74-fold), respectively, in contrast to the (BDL + quinacrine 5) treated group.

findings.evidence: Lean compiled a proof that the three hippocampal GFAP figures cannot all hold. Reductions of $33.9\%$ and $55.56\%$ relative to BDL force $X_{Q10}/X_{Q5} \geq 0.4443/0.6615 = 0.67188$, i.e. a between-dose drop of at most $\mathbf{32.83\%}$ (forced interval $32.71$–$32.83\%$), while the printed $\mathbf{33.33\%}$ requires $X_{Q10}/X_{Q5} \leq 0.66675$. The margin is about half a percentage point — small, but strictly outside every rounding of the two inputs. $33.33\%$ is an exact one-third, which suggests a round figure rather than one computed from the same two group means.

summary:
This is an experimental pharmacology paper (quinacrine against bile-duct-ligation-induced hepatic encephalopathy in rats) with **no display mathematics at all** — no equations, theorems, proofs or derivations. Its mathematically checkable content is the dense network of relative-change figures in the Results: for each of ~25 biomarkers the paper prints a BDL-vs-sham change, a change for each quinacrine dose relative to BDL, and a change of the 10 mg/kg dose relative to the 5 mg/kg dose. **The last figure is determined by the middle two**, so each biomarker carries a genuine arithmetic identity. I extracted 20 snippets, routed 16 to Lean and 4 to informal review.

Every Lean snippet settled: **13 PASSED, 3 REFUTED, 0 FAILED, 0 fallbacks needed.** Consistency was formalised as the *existence* of positive group means reproducing all three printed figures, with every figure allowed to be a rounding of its true value (half a unit in its last printed place); refutations are the negation of that, so none of them can be a rounding artefact. The method's calibration is good: on the tightest cases the forced interval and the printed figure agree to four significant figures (serum ammonia, $34.058$–$34.081\%$ vs printed $34.07\%$; hippocampal BMP2, $[1.4835, 1.4945]$ vs printed $1.49$; BDNF, $[1.7492, 1.7677]$ vs printed $1.76$).

**Three between-dose figures are formally refuted.** (1) *Hippocampal MDA* — the paper prints a $19.86\%$ drop where its own two preceding figures force exactly $25.0\%$; the liver figure in the same sentence ($43.66\%$) matches its derived value to four significant figures, so the convention is not in doubt and this is the clearest defect in the paper. (2) *Hippocampal WNT3A* — a printed $1.45$-fold between-dose rise against a forced ceiling of $1.365$, while the two sibling proteins in the same sentence (β-catenin, Lef1) are exact. (3) *Hippocampal GFAP* — a printed $33.33\%$ against a forced $32.71$–$32.83\%$; a half-point discrepancy, and $33.33\%$ is suspiciously an exact one-third. All three are **minor**: each is a redundant derived number in a Results paragraph, and none of them carries a conclusion — the direction and significance of every effect, and hence the paper's hepatoprotective and neuroprotective claims, survive intact.

The four informally reviewed snippets came back clean or unsettled, with two observations worth recording even though neither reaches the reporting threshold. The a priori power analysis checks out exactly: for $k=5$ groups, $\alpha = 0.05$ and Cohen's $f = 0.5$, power reaches $0.8526$ at $N=59$ and $0.8598$ at $N=60$, so the stated $60$ animals at $12$ per group is precisely what G*Power returns. The discrimination-index definition, however, is written with the subtraction reversed ("the difference in the amount of time consumed examining familiar and novel things"), which would make the BDL index positive and the treated indices negative — the opposite of what Section 3.3 reports; the quantity is still well defined and the slip does not propagate into any number. The escape-latency paragraph (paper::FORMULA_BLOCK::0) is the one snippet I could not settle either way: "reduction in escape latency by 27.4% and 47%, respectively" has no identifiable antecedent, and under the reading that these are dose-vs-dose figures they would contradict both the $29.9$–$30.9\%$ forced by the preceding sentence and the closing claim of "no noticeable distinction ... between the two doses". Because the referents are genuinely undetermined I recorded it as UNVERIFIABLE rather than as a finding.

Lean and the informal pass never disagreed: no snippet produced a FAILED verdict, so no Lean result needed an informal second opinion. The Lean project `MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper` was **reused, not created** (it already held a built Mathlib and other papers' proofs), so per `verify-math-lean`'s deletion rule it was kept; only this run's scratch (`TMP.lean`, `claim.md`) was removed, and the 16 proofs are saved under `Paper/Verified/0034-Quinacrine__*_opus5.lean`.
